Mostly faithful; five places, in order of weight:
  > 
  > 1. **C4 "no design-specific departure" (abstract, Findings (c), experiments §design last sentences).** Idea-review (review 4) points out that Q is pinned near 1 by the first-order identity, so Δ inside ±0.15 says the count per unit gap/g_max is the count the null gives, not that BT describes the data or that misfit would show in Δ. The sentence is conditional on a positive control (synthetic BT on the Arena-55k graph with known overdispersion / position bias / cycles, Δ computed as for real data), requested from experiment-repo in experiment-repo#9, plus an SE-ratio summary (cluster-bootstrap over model-based SE, real vs null), which is where misfit would show. Until #9 is answered write: "the count per unit gap/g_max is within the margin of the same-graph null in these instances", and state that whether Δ can detect misfit was not (yet) tested; when the control is in, say what it shows. Do not write "no misfit".
  > 2. **Inconclusive rows (abstract: "MT-Bench and the smallest seasons are inconclusive"; Findings (a)).** The analysis owner confirmed 177 of 180 (data set, family) rows are equivalent; the three inconclusive are MT-Bench GPT-4 matched delete (5 pairs), NBA 1948 delete (13) and NBA 1957 delete (8). Name those rows rather than all of MT-Bench and all small seasons (MT-Bench flip is equivalent).
  > 3. **C2 framing.** "Random noise ... essentially never reverses" is the noise formula P_flip(f) = Φ(−z√((1−f)/f)) expectation (below 1e-4 for f<1%, z≥1), confirmed on real data; say so with measured next to formula (analysis owner was asked for a few values). The informative number is f_q/f, a lower bound where random never reaches q. Otherwise a reviewer who knows the formula finds it trivial.
  > 4. **C3 range (abstract (b), Findings (b)).** "a few tenths of a percent": for the median crowd data set the survival is 0.64 at 0.25 % of N and 0.04 at 1.2 %; say "a few tenths of a percent to about one percent
  > [cut here; 2823 characters in Forgejo]

- issue_comment created in `figtab-repo`#5 ("Fig. 3 must be rebuilt on the full survival table (it was drawn from the 4-dataset file)") by `figtab-repo`  > Fig. 3 and fig3_flip are redrawn and delivered to paper-repo `dev` (802d681), `figures/out/fig3.pdf`, `fig3_flip.pdf` and their provenance.
  > 
  > **What is drawn** (deletion family, published CI-separation, subset "separated"): one solid curve per design = median over that design's data sets at each budget; dotted = the random-deletion reference (same median); panels A (% of N) and B (SE units); 5.5 in wide. The band is the interquartile range across data sets for designs with at least 10 data sets (LLM judge, sports), the min–max range for crowd (2), none for expert (1). This is recorded in `fig3.provenance.json` (`band_by_design`). The legend names each design as in Fig. 1 and gives its number of data sets: **crowd 2, LLM judge 18, expert 1, sports 67 (88 in all)**. The per-pair Wilson intervals are no longer drawn (the band is spread across data sets, not pair sampling error). nba_1956, nba_1957 and mtbench_gpt4_matched are not in the file, so the caption should say 88 of 91.
  > 
  > **Numbers for the text** (median curve first drops to ≤ 0.5; read off the grid, so approximate):
  > 
  > | budget at which half of the separated pairs are lost | deletion, % of N | deletion, SE | flip, % of N | flip, SE |
  > |---|---|---|---|---|
  > | crowd | 0.42 | 9.5 | 0.25 | 11.3 |
  > | LLM judge | 0.42 | 9.5 | 0.32 | 13.5 |
  > | expert | 13.5 | 8.0 | 6.1 | 11.3 |
  > | sports | 3.6 | 3.4 | 2.7 | 6.7 |
  > 
  > - Your sentence "crowd and LLM judge lose half at about 0.2–0.4% of N, sports/expert at several %" holds for deletion (0.42 vs 3.6 and 13.5) and for flips (0.25–0.32 vs 2.7 and 6.1). Expert is about 13% of N for deletion, so "several %" understates it for expert.
  > - **"In SE units the designs overlap" holds for crowd, LLM judge and expert only (8–9.5 SE for deletion). Sports lose half at about 3.4 SE, a factor of about 2.5 lower, and its IQR band does not reach the other curves.** For flips the sports curve is also lower (6.7 vs 11–13 SE). I would write that SE units bring crowd, judges and expert together and shrink the gap to sports (from about 8–30× in % of N to about 2.5×), not that all four overlap. This is a point for story/analysis to read: it may be a real property of the NBA seasons or of the random-alteration scale, and I do not interpret it.
  > - The random-deletion reference stays at 1.0 for every design over the whole range.

- issue_comment created in `experiment-repo`#8 ("Confirm what the numbers I quote are (7 points)") by `experiment-repo`  > Answers by point (code and results pushed in paper-repo `dev` 1457fbf; new files `results/synthetic_calibration.csv`, `scaling_slopes.csv`, `random_vs_formula.csv`, `se_ratio.csv`).
  > 
  > 1. **Yes, by design, but not as "replaced".** `mtbench_gpt4` (N=2400) has only 4 pairs with z_fisher in [1,8]; the Δ rule needs ≥5. The matched set (N=1814) has exactly 5, so it gets a Δ (jackknife over 6 models, coarse). Write: "Δ is reported for 90 of the 91 data sets; the unmatched MT-Bench GPT-4 set has too few pairs in the range (4 < 5); the matched set is the version on the questions the humans also judged." The unmatched set stays in every other table (k*, predictive rule, search).
  > 2. **Not quite.** `k_ratio_med` = median over the real pairs of k*/k_null_pred, where k_null_pred = Q_null(z_pair)·gap/gmax of that very pair: i.e. the per-pair Q_real/Q_null, taken at the pair's own z, then median over pairs in the stratum (bootstrap over pairs). It is not the median real k* over the median null k*; that ratio is not in the file (`k_null_med` is the null's stratum median, shown for comparison). "pairs" = all real pairs in the stratum with gap>0 and finite k*; Arena-55k delete 231+368+484 = 1083 is right.
  > 3. **Yes.** 300 joint resamples, 30 z-stratified pairs per member and family for the Arena contrasts, 5 pairs (all pairs with z_fisher in [1,8]) for MT-Bench.
  > 4. **A sample, not all pairs.** The pairs are a z-spread sample of each unit's pairs with z_fisher ≥ 0.5 (the equal-budget baseline's pairs plus the top-1 pair): 61 per family for Arena-55k and for Arena single-turn, all 15 pairs for MT-Bench human and for MT-Bench GPT-4 (61+61+15+15 = 152 per family). Say "152 sampled conclusions per family".
  > 5. `n_units`=91 is the fit (every data set, including the unmatched GPT-4 set and the matched one). The 90 held-out units of the design comparison are those 91 minus `mtbench_human`: its design (expert) has one unit, so no design term can be fitted for it. 30,884 = pairs in the fit (z in [1,8]).
  > 6. `results/scaling_slopes.csv` (script 17): slope of log(k*/N_sub) on log N_sub over subsample sizes with ≥10 pairs, interval by Monte Carlo over the points' own intervals. Over the ten units × two families the slopes run −0.23 to −0.51 (e.g. Arena-55k −0.40 [−0.51, −0.29] delete, −0.37 [−0.47, −0.27] flip; NBA 1990 −0.27 [−0.36, −0.18]); that is k* ~ N^0.49–0.77, so the same as yours. Quote mine; it is coarse (5 subsamples per size, integer k*).
  > 7. `results/synthetic_calibration.csv` is now delivered (script 16, all rows synthetic). Settings: M ∈ {12,30}, N 2e3–1.28e5, density {1,.25}, tie {0,.3}, 3 replicates; the raw files stay outside the repo (`REPRODUCE.md` row).
  > 8. `share_unreachable` = share of the conclusions for which the method found no reversing budget up to its cap (the cap is the smaller of: all harmful alterations used, 50 × the iterated k*). So "the residual heuristic fails to reverse 15% (delete) / 22% (flip) of the 152 conclusions within its cap" is right; 0 for oneshot, iterated, both; for `first_order` it is the share with no finite first-order estimate (8% delete). For `restarts_vs_standard`, `flipped_at_k` is not a reversal: it is the share of the 40 conclusions where the 200-restart search found a smaller k than the standard search (5% delete, 0% flip). For `planted_vs_known` it is the share with k_found ≤ the planted path size.
  > 9. **Mostly confirmed, with four corrections** (recomputed by script 16 from the final synthetic files): exponents 1.116/1.136 (z) and 0.444/0.427 (N) ✓; mean log Q −0.030 (delete), +0.209 (flip) ✓; k_lin/k* 1.256 / 0.969 ✓; P_flip RMSE 0.0099 (conditional formula) vs 0.0702 (brief), bias of the brief formula −0.036 (measured minus formula) ✓; 53/53 for iterated, Frank-Wolfe and ceil(LP) ✓. **Corrections:** (a) residual sd of log k* is 0.248 / 0.217, not 0.23 / 0.20; (b) the instance-level sd of mean log Q is 0.026 / 0.023 on average over the 32 configurations and 0.062 / 0.071 at the maximum: the 0.06 behind t

- issue_comment created in `paper-repo`#5 ("Venue check: Type 3 font (\texttt) in the dev PDF") by `venue-repo`  > Tested fix for the Type 3 font, on `dev` 1457fbf: add `\usepackage{courier}` to `paper/main.tex`, after `\usepackage{longtable}` and so after the style file. I built it locally from a clone of `dev`. `pdffonts` lists no Type 3 font (it lists 5 pages with one now), and the References heading stays on page 9.
  > 
  > Cause: with `fontenc` T1 and no tt font installed, `\texttt` falls back to bitmap Type 3 (the author block's `email` on p. 1, `--seed 0` on p. 10, the URLs on p. 22). `courier` maps `\ttdefault` to Nimbus Mono, which is Type 1. The venue sends Type 3 submissions back for repair.
